solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Opportunist coming upon two rivers

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
URE is a Yorkshire river and R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A chancer arrives at a spot where two rivers meet.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer can be a person who seeks gain by risky or unscrupulous means, a synonym for an opportunist.

clue.text: Forceful detectives arrested a lot on their return

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read in the opposite direction
the detectives hold the word for a lot inside, as captors

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
many means a lot

explanation.surface: Tough police officers nab lots of people when they get back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested' looks like the police at work, but it only signals one piece holding another; 'on their return' then reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means energetic and forceful, full of drive.

clue.text: Number of the chalet herewith

indicators.note: of here signals that the letters come out of the following words

explanation.surface: The number of the chalet is enclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a house or room number; it is something that numbs, an anaesthetic, from chalET HERewith.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early general anaesthetic, something that numbs: a 'numb-er'.

clue.text: Can metal be left in patient post-surgery?

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the clue word
after an operation things are rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Can a bit of metal be left in a patient after an operation?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L into PATIENT, then 'post-surgery' rearranges PATLIENT. 'Can' looks like a verb opening the question.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinplate is thin steel coated in tin, the sheet metal used for making food cans.

clue.text: Tracy and I creating new production; one of us is a shoo- in

indicators.note: a production makes something new from the parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two actors staging a new play, one tipped for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is not the signal but N; 'production' rearranges TRACY, I, CREATING and N. 'and' and 'one of us is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing certainty is a British idiom for something sure to happen, a sure winner, like a shoo-in.

clue.text: Insurrectionist in city about to start uprising

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city

indicators.note: in a down entry these letters read upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word to is taken

explanation.surface: A rebel in a city about to begin a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus T ('to start') gives RET, which 'uprising' turns to TER in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rioter is a person who takes part in a riot, a violent disturbance, so an insurgent.

clue.text: Longing, to some extent, for father

indicators.note: only part of the word for longing is used, its opening pair dropped

parts.note: a longing is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone yearns, in a measured way, for their dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' trims DE from DESIRE, leaving its last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to father offspring, and a sire is a male parent, especially of a horse.

clue.text: Got an exclusive about two students that searched for molluscs

indicators.note: the word for got an exclusive goes around the students

parts.note: a journalist who scooped rivals got an exclusive story
L is a learner, so two students give two Ls

explanation.surface: A reporter got a scoop about two students hunting shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Scollop is a variant spelling of scallop, the shellfish; 'Got an exclusive' is newspaper jargon for a scoop.
explanation.definitionFit: To scallop or scollop is to gather scallops, bivalve shellfish, so to hunt for them.

clue.text: Children on first make second edition

indicators.note: says the word for on comes before the word for children

parts.note: re means on or concerning
issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: Children top the bill when a book is released again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue a book is to publish it again, so to bring out another edition.

clue.text: Move slowly on island

definitions.meaning: to edge forward bit by bit
in Scotland and Ireland an ... is a small island

explanation.surface: Someone creeps along on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch as an island is a Scottish and Irish usage (from Gaelic innis), seen in names like Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Edging forward bit by bit is the verb sense; the noun is a Gaelic-derived word for a small isle.

clue.text: Alas, procession not as twice ordered at final stop

indicators.note: the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the word as is taken two times over, and not says those letters leave the pool

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad funeral procession, arranged without fuss, reaches its last stop.
explanation.walkthrough: From ALAS PROCESSION take away A, S, A, S ('not as twice'), and 'ordered' rearranges the remaining LPROCESION.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropolis is a large cemetery, the last resting place, so wryly a final stop.

clue.text: A lesson that's unprincipled

parts.note: the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: A lesson that teaches having no principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking moral principles or not caring about right and wrong; a near synonym.

clue.text: Points to one direction, which is uncalled-for

parts.note: needles have sharp points, so points can be needles
S is south, one compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone pointing to one way, which nobody asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnecessary and gratuitous is uncalled-for; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: A bird calls for a moment, heard without amplification

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: A bird calls for a moment
parts.note: A, then COOS for a dove's calls, then TICK for a moment

explanation.surface: A bird briefly calls, and is heard without a microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link: A COO'S TICK, said out loud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An acoustic instrument or performance is unplugged, using no electric amplification.

clue.text: Real fungi need to be cultivated

indicators.note: cultivating changes how things grow, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Genuine mushrooms need to be grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real' looks like an adjective on 'fungi'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfeigned means sincere and not pretended, so genuine or real.

clue.text: Catch sight of wee Kelvin

parts.note: wee and pee are both childish words for urine
K is the symbol for the kelvin unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Glimpsing little Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like the Scottish 'small', but it is urination.
explanation.definitionFit: To peek is to take a quick look, roughly glimpsing something.

clue.text: Where Robin and Martin get clean away with it?

definitions.text: Where Robin and Martin get clean away with it?

parts.words: Where Robin and Martin get clean away with it?
parts.note: Robin and Martin look like two men escaping justice, but they are birds and 'get clean' means wash

explanation.walkthrough: Robin and martin are both garden birds, and the place where birds wash is a garden basin. 'Get clean away' reads as escaping.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow garden basin of water is where small birds such as robins and martins bathe.

clue.text: Argument about lunch is not popular

indicators.note: the word for popular is absent from the meal

parts.note: tiffin is a light midday meal, from British India
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A row about a lunch that is not well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: TIFFIN is an Anglo-Indian word for a light lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a small argument.

clue.text: Type to emphasise it's about the girl, mainly

indicators.note: the clue word goes around the girl's name

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: most of the name is used, the final letter dropped

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name, as in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A slanted typeface used for stress, it's about the girl largely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of the name, and 'about' wraps the clue's own 'it's' around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping typeface is used in print to stress or emphasise words.

clue.text: Artist going down for a little water

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
in drop: in descent, falling

explanation.surface: A painter is descending in search of a bit of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going down' is read as IN DROP, being in a drop or fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling drop of rain is a small quantity of water.

clue.text: Opening scripture lesson in workplace after first fellow's gone

indicators.note: the scripture lesson goes inside the shortened workplace
the first of the two fellows is the one removed
the fellow has gone, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: an office is a place of work
RI is religious instruction, a school scripture lesson

explanation.surface: Starting a Bible class at the office after the first man has left.
explanation.walkthrough: The workplace word holds two Fs; 'after first fellow's gone' removes just one. RI, Religious Instruction, is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening, such as a mouth or a vent; a synonym.

clue.text: Old physician loses container of animals

indicators.note: the container is taken out of the physician's name

parts.note: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek father of medicine
a crate is a container

explanation.surface: An ancient doctor misplaces a box of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes CRATE from HIPPOCRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippos, short for hippopotamuses, are large African mammals, examples of animals.

clue.text: Unsophisticated trainee one's taken into a church

indicators.note: the trainee and one are placed inside the word for simple

parts.note: basic means simple and unrefined
L is a learner, as on an L-plate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A naive apprentice is brought into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is 'one has', so 'taken into' puts LI inside BASIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church with a central nave, or one given special papal privileges.

clue.text: Works hard to be into crime!

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking or being into it
a sin is a wrong or offence

explanation.surface: Exclaiming that keen effort means being drawn to wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is idiom for setting to work in earnest, applying oneself hard.

clue.text: Court attention-seeker

parts.note: reads as someone showing off at court, but it is the judge's tool rapped for order

explanation.walkthrough: 'attention-seeker' suggests a show-off; here it is the object a judge bangs to get the court's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or auctioneer raps a small mallet to call a room to order and gain its attention.

clue.text: Adapting an eccentric animal

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd animal adjusting to its surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bamboo-eating bear of China is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Cover very expensive in lace originally

indicators.note: originally points to the starting letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A costly lacy covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a piece of fabric that covers the face, or anything that conceals; a cover.

clue.text: Exploited after having ushered the lady out

indicators.note: the word for the lady is taken out of the clue word

parts.note: her refers to a woman, the lady

explanation.surface: Someone feels taken advantage of after showing a woman out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HER from USHERED, as 'out' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exploited is to be used, taken advantage of; a synonym.

clue.text: Report to tell of missiles found on island group

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so what follows is said out loud

parts.note: SAY means tell; shells are artillery missiles; 'of' just joins them

explanation.surface: A news report about rockets discovered on some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: SAY SHELLS spoken sounds like the answer; 'Report' also pretends to be a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seychelles is an archipelago republic in the Indian Ocean, a group of islands.
